result.rationale: The finding's threat model is contradicted by the diff: postMessageReceived guards with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, so only messages originating from the Discourse forum's own domain are processed. A 'malicious embedder' (the third-party site embedding the iframe) cannot send the discourse-resize message and thus cannot influence e.data.height; only the trusted Discourse origin can. Assigning an unvalidated string to iframe.height from the trusted origin is not a security defect, leaving this a vague validation preference.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js the height is set from postMessage data, but messages are accepted only when `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) !== -1`, i.e., only from the Discourse iframe’s origin, not from the embedding parent (“malicious embedder” can’t satisfy this origin check). Also, assigning `iframe.height = e.data.height + "px"` sets a DOM attribute value, not HTML, so the claim of “inject arbitrary strings into the iframe height attribute” as a security issue is overstated given what the diff shows.
